archetype.name: Fringe Contender (weak-division lifeline)
archetype.definition: A below-average team by efficiency whose only realistic path to January runs through an NFC East where nobody has pulled away. Turnovers have kept it close, and injuries are now draining the roster that would have to make the climb.

report.headline: Turnover luck kept Washington afloat; injuries and a leaky secondary threaten to sink it.
report.take:
Washington is 2-4-1 and has been outscored 159-182. That -23 differential implies about 3.1 wins, so the record is roughly honest. This is not an unlucky good team. Net EPA sits 25th, the offense is 18th by EPA and the defense 25th. History says the 2024 breakout (12 wins, a fourth-ranked offense) was the outlier. The 2025 drop to five wins and a 31st-ranked defense looks more like the baseline this group keeps returning to.

The one thing propping it up is the ball. The offense has turned it over only three times against ten takeaways, a +7 margin that ranks third in the league per game. That is how a team with the 25th-ranked success rate and the 29th-ranked defensive success rate allowed stays in games. It is how Seattle became a 33-31 win despite giving up 393 passing yards, and how the 27-27 tie with the Giants happened. Margins like that rarely hold over a full season. When they shrink, the underlying team shows.

That underlying team has a split identity. The offensive line opens real lanes: 3.21 yards before contact ranks second. Yet the backs finish at 3.71 a carry, 21st, which says the runners are leaving yards on the field rather than the blocking failing. Pass protection is the opposite problem. A 0.254 pressure rate (28th) with Laremy Tunsil on IR all season has left Jayden Daniels under fire. On defense, offenses simply throw. Washington is the league's strongest pass funnel, its pass EPA allowed ranks 26th, and it converts red-zone trips into touchdowns at the worst rate in the league (0.818). The run defense and short-area coverage are solid, but the deep middle and the tight end are open.

Where it goes now depends on the injury report as much as the scheme. Terry McLaurin is out for the year with a torn patellar tendon. Daron Payne needs foot surgery, Javon Kinlaw is out and Jer'Zhan Newton is on IR, which strips the interior line that kept runs from breaking. The division keeps the door ajar. With a gauntlet of Minnesota, Jacksonville and Cincinnati on the back half, though, this looks like a team scrapping for six or seven wins rather than a sleeper.

strengths.title: Protecting the football, taking it away
strengths.body: Daniels-led offenses have coughed it up just three times all year while the defense has ten takeaways. That margin is the single biggest reason Washington has been in nearly every game. Low giveaway rates have some staying power with a careful quarterback. The takeaway side is more random, so expect the margin to narrow rather than vanish.

strengths.title: Line wins the point of attack
strengths.body: Washington's backs average 3.21 yards before anyone touches them, second in the league, and the team converts 75% of short-yardage tries. When the backs finish runs, the ground game takes over, as in the 202-yard day against the Giants. The gap between blocking and final yards per carry points to the runners. That makes the run game a fixable problem rather than a structural one.

strengths.title: Few explosive runs, tight underneath
strengths.body: The defense allows explosive runs at the second-lowest rate in the league and is sixth in EPA on short passes. It rallies and tackles in front of it. The caveat is that the interior linemen who anchored that run defense are now mostly sidelined, so this is the strength most at risk going forward.

concerns.title: Pass defense invites the air attack
concerns.body: Offenses throw against Washington more than against anyone relative to the situation, and with good reason. Pass EPA allowed ranks 26th, deep EPA allowed 20th, and opposing top tight ends have feasted at the worst rate in the league. Then the red zone finishes the job: 0.818 of trips end in touchdowns, last in the league. This matches the 2025 unit, so it looks like a real flaw, not a slow start.

concerns.title: Injuries hollow both lines' strengths
concerns.body: Payne (74% of snaps) is done until February, Kinlaw is out, and Newton is on IR, which takes most of the defensive tackle rotation off the field. On offense, McLaurin's knee surgery ends his season and Tunsil has not played a snap. These are not depth hits. They remove the players the team's best traits were built on.

concerns.title: Pressure is getting to Daniels
concerns.body: Washington allows pressure on 0.254 of dropbacks and QB hits at the 28th-ranked rate. Its time to throw is among the longer marks in the league, so some of that is Daniels holding the ball. The Giants got five sacks in the tie. Without Tunsil, expect this to persist. It also matters beyond one game: the lone Mariota start produced -9.5 passing EPA, so Daniels' health is the season.

trend.note: Close losses to Philadelphia and San Francisco and a shootout win over Seattle bracket a lopsided loss in Mariota's lone start and a tie with the Giants. The bye was followed by the most complete game of the year, a 27-10 win with five sacks, though it came against the league's 30th-ranked offense.

nextGame.headline: Better-than-its-record Rams bring the passing game Washington can't stop
nextGame.body:
The Rams are 4-4, but their net EPA ranks sixth and their wins-over-expected ranks 30th: they have played like a good team that lost close ones. Their offense leans on the pass more than most and has elite protection (pressure allowed 2nd) and run blocking (stuff rate 1st). That is the worst possible pairing for a Washington defense that funnels everything to the air and gives up touchdowns in the red zone. On the other side, the Rams' defense is fourth in EPA and best in the league against deep throws, but it barely pressures the quarterback. Daniels can get comfortable if he takes what's underneath. The Book has the Rams by 5.5 with a 47.5 total.

Availability swings both ways. Matthew Stafford is questionable with arm soreness after the Chargers game, and both starting corners, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, are questionable. Davante Adams is on IR and tight end Colby Parkinson is out, which blunts the tight-end matchup Washington usually loses. Myles Garrett is on track to practice, and his return would change the pressure picture fast. The Rams' long snapper, Joe Cardona, is out on a special-teams unit that already ranks last. For Washington, the defensive tackle room is gutted with Payne and Kinlaw out and Newton on IR. McLaurin is gone, and Jeremy McNichols is doubtful.

waysToWin.title: Win the turnover battle again
waysToWin.body: Washington is third in turnover margin per game, and the Rams are 27th with only six takeaways. If Daniels keeps the ball safe and the defense steals a possession or two, that offsets the efficiency gap the way it did against Seattle.

waysToWin.title: Steal hidden yards on special teams
waysToWin.body: The Rams rank dead last in special-teams EPA per game and are playing without their long snapper. Washington's units are only 25th themselves. Still, a botched snap, a blocked kick or a short field is a realistic swing in a game the Book sees as a field goal and change.

waysToWin.title: Live underneath, attack the third receiver
waysToWin.body: The Rams own the league's best deep-pass defense but rank 25th in pressure rate, so Daniels should get time to work short and intermediate. Opposing third receivers have outscored their averages against the Rams at the second-worst rate in the league. With McLaurin out, getting Antonio Williams or Treylon Burks into that role is the cleanest matchup on the board, especially if the Rams' corners are limited.

waysToLose.title: Stafford carves the pass funnel
waysToLose.body: A pass-heavy Rams offense with a clean pocket meets the defense opponents most like to throw on, one that ranks 26th in pass EPA allowed. If Stafford's arm is fine, long drives that end in touchdowns are the default script. Washington's last-ranked red-zone defense turns field goals into sevens.

waysToLose.title: Rams run through missing tackles
waysToLose.body: Los Angeles has the league's lowest stuff rate and averages 4.73 yards a carry. Washington's run defense was built on an interior trio that is now largely sidelined. If the explosive-run prevention cracks, the Rams can play keep-away with both phases working.

waysToLose.title: Offense stalls on early downs
waysToLose.body: The Rams rank sixth in rush EPA allowed and fifth on third down. Washington's offense ranks 25th in success rate and its backs already struggle to finish runs. If first and second down go nowhere, Daniels faces third-and-long behind a line allowing pressure at the 28th-ranked rate.

nextGame.watch: Stafford's arm and whether Myles Garrett returns. A limited Stafford makes this a coin flip. A healthy Stafford with Garrett back gives the Rams the edge in nearly every phase.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect regression in the one area that has carried Washington. A +7 turnover margin with only three giveaways is unlikely to hold, and without it this profile resembles the 2025 team more than the 2024 one. The injuries are not the kind a team schemes around. Losing McLaurin narrows a passing game already short on efficiency, and losing most of the defensive tackle rotation threatens the run defense, the unit's one dependable trait. The pass defense and red-zone problems have now persisted across two seasons.

The schedule offers soft spots: Tennessee at 1-7, plus Houston, Arizona and Atlanta with losing records. It also closes with Minnesota, Jacksonville and Cincinnati-caliber opponents and two division games. A weak NFC East keeps the playoff door technically open, but the likelier finish is a team hovering around six wins. A healthy Daniels is the floor-raiser, and a late Tunsil return is the only meaningful reinforcement in sight.
swingFactors: Daniels staying healthy (the Mariota start was the season's worst game)
How far the turnover margin regresses
Run defense holding up without Payne, Kinlaw and Newton

confidence.note: Seven games is a small sample, and season-ending injuries to McLaurin and Payne change the roster the numbers describe.
